title: Custom PopupMenu stays open when clicking outside on desktop or workspace

environment.extra: Wayland and X11 GNOME Shell Sessions

symptoms: Custom PopupMenu or popover remains open when clicking outside on another window, background, or panel
Closing popup synchronously on notify::focus-window causes Error: incorrect pop race condition
expected_behavior: Clicking outside an active context menu closes all open menus cleanly while letting the target click propagate
trigger: Open a custom PopupMenu and click outside on a workspace window or background
root_cause: Custom PopupMenus outside Main.panel.menuManager lack global stage click interception. Synchronous closing inside focus-window handlers interferes with Mutter's active menu pop stack.

failed_approaches.result: Throws Error: incorrect pop because menu state mutates during focus dispatch

fix_summary: Attach captured-event listener to global.stage. On BUTTON_PRESS outside menu actor bounds, schedule menu dismissal via GLib.idle_add(GLib.PRIORITY_DEFAULT, ...) and return Clutter.EVENT_PROPAGATE.

manual_steps: Right click to open dock context menu
Click outside on a workspace window or background
Verify menu closes cleanly and target window receives focus

regression_risks: Captured-event listener leaking memory if not disconnected in disable()

title: Extension preferences window fails to open or doesn't raise to front on repeated click

environment.extra: Wayland and X11 GNOME Shell Sessions

symptoms: Clicking extension settings button throws JS signature error across GNOME Shell versions
Clicking settings button when window is already open does nothing instead of focusing it
expected_behavior: Clicking settings button opens prefs window or raises existing prefs window to front across all GNOME Shell versions
trigger: Click settings button in extension UI
root_cause: Signature differences in Main.extensionManager.openExtensionPrefs across GNOME 42 vs 45 vs 46, and lack of window list check before spawning new process.

failed_approaches.approach: Calling openExtensionPrefs(uuid) without version fallback or window focus check
failed_approaches.result: Throws error on GNOME 45+ or opens redundant duplicate windows

fix_summary: Iterate Meta.TabList.NORMAL via global.display.get_tab_list. If prefs window is open, unminimize, activate workspace, and call Main.activateWindow. If not open, call openExtensionPrefs with Util.spawn fallback.

manual_steps: Click Settings button in dock
Verify prefs window opens
Minimize or move window behind other windows, then click Settings button again
Verify existing prefs window raises to front and receives focus

regression_risks: Failing to match window wm_class or title

title: Dock extension fails to hide or stays visible over fullscreen games during Alt+Tab
symptoms: Dock stays visible over fullscreen game windows when switching windows via Alt+Tab
Mouse polling or raise_top() calls periodically pull the dock back onto the screen during fullscreen gameplay
expected_behavior: Dock hides completely (hide() and reactive = false) whenever a fullscreen window is active on the monitor, ignoring mouse triggers until fullscreen mode exits
trigger: Switch focus to a fullscreen game window using Alt+Tab or launch a game in fullscreen mode
root_cause: Listening solely to notify::fullscreen or in-fullscreen-changed on individual window actors fails when focus transitions between windows via Alt+Tab without window property mutation. Additionally, trackFullscreen: true without actor.hide(), reactive = false, and barrier destruction allows mouse edge polling and raise_top() calls to re-show the dock over fullscreen games.

failed_approaches.approach: Connecting only to in-fullscreen-changed signal on Meta.Window
failed_approaches.result: Fails on Alt+Tab because window fullscreen property does not change when focus shifts to an existing fullscreen window

failed_approaches.approach: Moving dock position off-screen via ease({ x: monitor.width })
failed_approaches.result: Mouse polling and pressure barrier callbacks bring the dock back on screen after 100ms

fix_summary: Implement FullscreenController listening to global.display signals notify::focus-window, in-fullscreen-changed, and restacked with GLib.idle_add debouncing. Validate focused window fullscreen state and get_monitor_in_fullscreen(). On fullscreen, invoke hide(), reactive = false, and destroy barriers.

manual_steps: Launch a fullscreen application or game
Use Alt+Tab to switch focus to and from the fullscreen application
Move the mouse cursor to the right monitor edge and verify the dock remains completely hidden and non-interactive
Exit fullscreen mode and verify dock visibility restores immediately

regression_risks: Dock remaining permanently hidden after exiting a crashed game
Pressure barriers failing to re-initialize after exiting fullscreen

title: Context menu switches to adjacent items on hover due to shared PopupMenuManager

environment.extra: Wayland and X11 GNOME Shell Sessions

symptoms: After opening a context menu (app icon or stolen tray indicator), moving the mouse pointer across adjacent icons immediately closes the current menu and opens the menu of the hovered icon without clicking
Moving the mouse cursor to click a lower menu item in a tray menu triggers the main panel context menu instead
expected_behavior: Context menus open strictly on an explicit right-click action and never switch automatically upon hovering over adjacent icons or panel areas
trigger: Open a context menu on an app icon or stolen tray indicator, then move the mouse cursor across adjacent icons or panel space
root_cause: Main.panel.menuManager (an instance of PopupMenuManager) implements active menu hover-cycling designed for top panel menu bars (File -> Edit -> View). Registering custom extension PopupMenus or stolen statusArea indicators in Main.panel.menuManager activates hover-switching across all registered actors. Additionally, attaching right-click listeners to the root container (_dockContainer) receives event bubbling from all child branches in Clutter.

failed_approaches.approach: Returning Clutter.EVENT_STOP on root container button-press-event for tray icons
failed_approaches.result: Cancels Clutter pointer grab and suppresses button-release-event and clicked signals on target children, making tray icons unresponsive
Intercepts and blocks normal left-clicks on tray icons whenever an indicator menu is open

fix_summary: Call Main.panel.menuManager.removeMenu(indicator.menu) on stolen indicators and avoid registering extension menus with Main.panel.menuManager. Move right-click background listeners from root container to _appsScrollView, mark interactive actors with _blocksDockContextMenu = true, and debounce single-turn menu closes via GLib.idle_add.

manual_steps: Right click an app icon or stolen tray indicator to open its context menu
Move the mouse pointer over adjacent tray icons and app icons without pressing any button
Verify that no adjacent context menu opens on hover
Click menu items or click outside to verify clean dismissal

regression_risks: Stolen tray indicator menus not closing when clicking outside
Interference between app icon context menus and panel background context menu

title: Stolen statusArea indicators distorted or misaligned in custom grid

environment.extra: Wayland and X11 GNOME Shell Sessions

symptoms: Stolen GNOME Shell statusArea indicators render stretched, oversized, or misaligned with huge padding in custom tray grid
expected_behavior: Stolen tray indicators preserve active state and render cleanly in 32x32px slots inside a 3-column row grid
trigger: Remove indicator actors from Main.panel._rightBox or statusArea and add them directly to a custom St.BoxLayout or St.Bin
root_cause: Indicators inherit top-panel theme rules (-natural-hpadding, -minimum-hpadding) and container alignment parameters from Main.panel._rightBox. Adding them directly to custom containers without state saving, CSS resets, and size constraining distorts layout.

failed_approaches.approach: Direct re-parenting without saving original properties or applying CSS overrides
failed_approaches.result: Icons render overflowing 32px constraints with unequal padding

fix_summary: Save actor state (x_align, y_align, style), constrain sizes recursively (constrainActorRecursive), wrap in 32x32px TrayIconWrapper with clip_to_allocation: false, and apply CSS resets (-natural-hpadding: 0; margin: 0; padding: 0;).

manual_steps: Launch applications with status indicators (Telegram, Steam, Discord)
Verify indicator icons align in 32x32px slots in a 3-column grid
Disable extension and verify indicators return to default top panel undamaged

regression_risks: Indicator signals breaking upon return to top panel

title: Hiding top panel with opacity=0 leaves an invisible top dead zone

environment.extra: Wayland and X11 GNOME Shell Sessions

symptoms: Top panel is transparent, but top 32px of monitor is unresponsive to window clicks or window title drag
expected_behavior: Top panel is completely removed from layout, allowing windows to occupy the top 32px seamlessly
trigger: Attempting to hide GNOME Shell top panel using Main.panel.opacity = 0
root_cause: Setting Main.panel.opacity = 0 makes the actor transparent, but leaves it registered in Mutter layout manager and input region. The top panel continues occupying ~32px physical height.

failed_approaches.result: Panel is invisible but continues blocking mouse events and occupying layout space

fix_summary: Replace Main.panel.opacity = 0 with Main.panel.hide() and Main.panel.reactive = false. Restore with Main.panel.show() and Main.panel.reactive = true.

manual_steps: Enable extension
Move application window to the very top edge of the screen
Verify mouse clicks on the top window title bar work cleanly

regression_risks: Failing to call Main.panel.show() in disable(), leaving user without top panel

title: Custom popup or window preview is visible but mouse clicks pass through to underlying windows

environment.extra: Wayland and X11 GNOME Shell Sessions

symptoms: Custom popover or window preview card is rendered on screen but ignores mouse clicks
Clicks pass through the preview card and activate elements in windows underneath
expected_behavior: Custom popover/preview card captures mouse hover and button clicks reliably
trigger: Add a floating popover actor to Main.uiGroup without registering it in Mutter input region
root_cause: Adding an actor via Main.uiGroup.add_actor() places it in the visual scene graph, but does not include its bounds in Mutter's interactive input region. Mutter filters pointer events based on its tracked input region mask.

failed_approaches.approach: Setting reactive: true and track_hover: true on St.BoxLayout
failed_approaches.result: Clutter actor parameters do not override Mutter input region masking

fix_summary: Register the popup actor using Main.layoutManager.addTopChrome(popup, { affectsInputRegion: true, trackFullscreen: true }). Additionally, set button_mask: St.ButtonMask.ONE on interactive St.Button children.

manual_steps: Hover an app icon to show the window preview popup
Click close or maximize buttons on the preview card
Verify the button action executes and clicks do not pass through to background windows

regression_risks: Failing to remove TopChrome actor upon hide/destroy, causing invisible input blocks

title: Maximized windows extend under custom GNOME Shell panel or dock

environment.extra: Wayland and X11 GNOME Shell Sessions

symptoms: Maximized application windows slide underneath the custom panel/dock
Resizing windows manually pushes window title bars under the panel
expected_behavior: Mutter reserves screen edge space according to dock width and automatically constrains maximized/tiled application windows outside the dock area
trigger: Add a custom panel to GNOME Shell and maximize any application window
root_cause: Adding a custom panel actor using Main.layoutManager.addChrome() without specifying affectsStruts: true. Mutter's layout manager remains unaware that screen edge space must be reserved and does not emit _NET_WM_STRUT_PARTIAL window constraints.

failed_approaches.approach: Setting custom window workarea constraints in JavaScript manually
failed_approaches.result: Overridden by Mutter window manager during workspace restacking and window creation

fix_summary: Pass affectsStruts: true in Main.layoutManager.addChrome(dockActor, { affectsStruts: true, affectsInputRegion: true, trackFullscreen: true }). Mutter automatically creates and manages window struts for the panel actor.

manual_steps: Enable the extension panel
Open any window (e.g. Terminal or Browser) and click Maximize
Verify the right edge of the window stops cleanly at the left boundary of the panel

regression_risks: Struts staying registered after hiding dock in autohide mode (handled by removing chrome or setting affectsStruts dynamically)
